uncited: *   **Inputs:** 3D volumetric data (scalar field), viewing parameters (camera position, orientation), transfer function (mapping data values to color/opacity), and rendering mode.
*   *3D Texture:* A single volume texture object.
**Proxy Geometry:** A set of 2D polygons (quads or triangle fans) representing slices through the volume bounding box.
*   *For 3D Textures (View-Aligned):* Define slicing planes perpendicular to the viewing direction.
Intersect these planes with the volume bounding box edges.
Sort the resulting intersection vertices in clockwise or counter-clockwise order around the slice centroid.
Interpolate texture coordinates from vertex attributes.
Perform data texture lookup using interpolated coordinates to get data value $d$.
Use $d$ as texture coordinates for a dependent lookup into the transfer function texture to get color $C$ and opacity $A$.
Send result to the compositing stage (blending).
*   **Sampling Rate ($s$):** Inversely proportional to sample distance $l$.
*   **Sampling Rate Dependence:** The sampling rate depends on the volume resolution.
*   **Time Complexity:** Depends on the number of slices and the resolution of the texture lookup.
*   **Memory Complexity:** 3D textures use less memory (no replication).
*   **When to Use:** When hardware supports 3D textures or 2D texture stacks and the scene requires interactive frame rates with moderate volume resolution.
